question: simple-login.web confirms booking-api@v1 consumers [simple-login.web.5, simple-login.web.7, simple-login.web.8, simple-login.web.9]; the front matter's other consumer, simple-login.integration.3, is still DEC-053's guess for a phase H18 has not planned. How does the confirm land, and do phase_ids and status move?

options.label: replace the web ids, keep the integration guess, stay provisional and draft
options.consequence: consumers become [simple-login.web.5, simple-login.web.7, simple-login.web.8, simple-login.web.9, simple-login.integration.3]; hsdd-config keeps warning (C7) that booking-api@v1 is draft and provisional until H19 confirms the integration side; the flip waits one more reconcile

options.label: replace the web ids and flip to final and stable now
options.consequence: the web lane builds against a stable contract one reconcile earlier, but phase_ids final would name simple-login.integration.3, a phase that does not exist yet, breaking the rule that final ids are planned phases

options.label: replace the web ids and drop the integration guess
options.consequence: the consumer list holds only planned phases, but the integration node, a known consumer of booking-api@v1 (PRD v2 Success tests), vanishes from the front matter and the root's contract matrix until H19, and C7 stops tracking it

chosen: replace the web ids, keep the integration guess, stay provisional and draft
why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 flips phase_ids to final only when both producer and consumer ids are confirmed; the producer side was confirmed at S17 (simple-login.backend.7), this node's side now is, but the integration side is a guessed id for a phase that hsdd/spec/simple-login.integration.md does not have (it ends at simple-login.integration.2), and the integration node has planned consumers to come (intake record H18), so the 'no planned phase consumers counts as confirmed' clause does not apply. The confirm replaces only this node's ids; the integration id is that node's to confirm at H19, as the confirm's own sub-bullet says. Step 7 then leaves status draft because phase_ids is not final, though the schema and all 35 fixtures exist. An integration plan that consumed no booking-api@v1 fixture would have changed my mind toward treating its side as confirmed.

question: profile-api@v2 and auth-api@v1 are stable with phase_ids final; simple-login.web confirms new consumer phases for both (web.5, web.7, web.8 for profile-api@v2; web.8 for auth-api@v1), while simple-login.integration's appended phases (H18) will likely consume both too and are not listed yet. Are the ids added in place with phase_ids left final, or do both contracts go back to provisional until H19?

options.label: add the ids in place, phase_ids stays final
options.consequence: both contracts stay stable and final; the front matter names every planned consumer phase so far, and H19 adds the integration node's when it confirms them; no contract body or version moves

options.label: add the ids and reopen phase_ids to provisional until H19
options.consequence: the front matter would signal that consumer ids may still change, but hsdd-config would warn every consumer of two contracts whose interface has not moved, and no rule of hsdd-reconcile reverses a flip

chosen: add the ids in place, phase_ids stays final
why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 applies a confirm to produced_by and consumers and only ever flips provisional to final; step 7 does not re-examine contracts that were already stable. phase_ids final means the listed ids are real planned phases, which every added id is (the web plan's phases 5, 7 and 8 exist and name these versions in their Consumes lines). The integration node's future consumers join at its own reconcile, as simple-login.web.4 and simple-login.integration.2 joined profile-api@v2 after it was final. Adding consumer ids is front matter only, not an amend: no guarantee, shape, schema or fixture changes, so no Versioning line and no version question arise. A rule that final means no consumer may be added later would have changed my mind.

question: The version ripple adds booking-api@v1 to simple-login.web's Consumes and to every copy above it. The root's child-node table also gives the web's Purpose as "the Login and Home screens in the browser", which the header (H7) has outgrown with Rooms, bookings and time zones. Does this reconcile rewrite that cell?

options.label: leave the cell, as DEC-153 did for the backend row
options.consequence: the table's Consumes and the embedded summary match the header; the Purpose cell stays stale until an hsdd-spec touch on simple-login, which S17 already routed to the run as a consider covering both rows

options.label: rewrite the cell from the header's Purpose
options.consequence: the row reads current now, but reconcile writes a summary hsdd-spec owns, and the backend row, left by DEC-153, stays stale beside it, so the table becomes inconsistent in a new way

chosen: leave the cell, as DEC-153 did for the backend row
why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 names the copied fields as Produces, Consumes and Sources, and its quality gate checks those; S17 found (DEC-153) that the Purpose column was never a verbatim copy of each header, so it is hsdd-spec's summary. Treating the web row as S17 treated the backend row keeps the two reconciles consistent, and S17's routed consider already names both rows, so no second item is routed. An owner instruction that reconcile keeps every column of the child table current would have changed my mind.

question: S19 drained the web's three confirms, rippled booking-api@v1 into the web's Consumes and the root's copies, and left booking-api@v1 draft and provisional for H19. Its reads outside are the run's records. Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The web is reconciled; H18 and H19 settle the integration consumer and can flip booking-api@v1 to stable.

why: Every change is a confirm or the version ripple reconcile owns; the auth-api consumer mismatch on shipped web.3 and web.4 is history, already the open execution plan's C-3 owner question. All reads are inside the repository; none is out of bounds. A collision or an unfounded consumer id would have changed this.
